title: LeapAttack: Hard-Label Adversarial Attack on Text via Gradient-Based Optimization

problem.claim: Generating text adversarial examples in the hard-label setting is a realistic and challenging black-box attack problem because gradients cannot be directly calculated from discrete word replacements.

gap.claim: The effectiveness of gradient-based methods for hard-label text attacks still requires improvement.

contributions.claim: LeapAttack is a gradient-based optimization method for crafting text adversarial examples in the hard-label setting.
LeapAttack represents semantic deviation between substituted words as difference vectors in word embedding space and uses an iterative gradient-estimation and substitution procedure.

author_reported_evidence.claim: In the general case, the authors report that LeapAttack efficiently generates high-quality text adversarial examples with the highest semantic similarity and lowest perturbation rate among the compared hard-label setting results.

narrative_sequence.summary: Hard-label text adversarial example generation is challenging because gradients are unavailable for discrete word replacements.
Existing gradient-based methods need improved effectiveness for this problem.
The paper proposes LeapAttack, which uses embedding-space difference vectors to characterize semantic deviation.
LeapAttack estimates gradients after moving near the decision boundary, then maps the estimated direction to substitution words using cosine similarity in an iterative process.
The authors report strong efficiency, semantic similarity, and perturbation-rate results in the general case.

source_observation.claim: Representing discrete word substitutions as continuous difference vectors enables gradient-based optimization in a hard-label text attack.

interpretation.claim: A continuous surrogate representation can make gradient information usable when the original decision variables are discrete.

application.claim: For other discrete optimization problems, consider embedding or difference-vector representations that preserve the relevant semantic or task-space relationships.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this representation works beyond the reported text attack setting.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, exact metrics, numerical results, query costs, and experimental conditions are not specified.
The abstract does not report limitations, failure cases, or performance outside the general case.
